full_judgment:
The facts of the cases in short, are that the writ-petitioners in the cases are a Joint Venture Company operating in Bangladesh and involved in construction of different infrastructures etc. under the different projects taken by the Government as well under foreign aided projects. The writ-petitioners formed the Joint Venture by executing joint venture agreement with China Harbour Engineering Company for bidding and executing different projects of the Roads and Highways Departments under the Ministry of Communication. The writ-petitioners as per the invitation of bid for improvement and construction of 3rd Road and Rehabilitation and Maintenance Project submitted bid and a pre-bid was held on 3-12-1999. Subsequently, the writ-petitioners executed contracts on 24-5-2000 and 5-7-2000 respectively for the projects in question as per the contract data. The notice to proceed was issued on 5-7-2000 and 6-6-2000 respectively. The completion date was fixed on 5-1-2003 in respect of the work of Writ Petition No.7124 of 2003 and on 5-8-2002 and 5-1-2004 in respect of work of Writ Petition No.714 I of 2004. The formal possession was handed over in the month of August, 2000 though the actual possession of the site was handed over in the month of December, 2002. The employer also issued a letter admitting non-delivery of possession of the site area. Subsequently, several correspondences were made between the parties and also the employer admitted the delay in handing over the site as well as other reasons and variation orders were duly approved by the employer. Again the writ-petitioners applied for variation and second variation was also duly approved by the employer considering the delay in handing over the site to the writ-petitioners. As the writ-petitioners were preparing proposal for extension of time for implementing the second variation as already approved by the employer, all of a sudden, the employer issued final notices on 13-7-2003 in respect of the subject matters of both the writ petitions. The writ-petitioners replied to the said final notices and also sent representation to the concerned Ministry for taking necessary action. The concerned Ministry, namely, Ministry of Communication sent a letter to the Chief Engineer as well as Project Manager asking clarification. Keeping the correspondences pending the impugned orders were passed by the writ-respondents terminating the contract and writ-respondent No. 3 directed the concerned Bank to encash the respective guarantees submitted by the contractor as per the contract data. 

 13. Leave was granted to consider whether because of inadequate resources, poor management and shortage of technical staff the work could not be completed and whether the Chief Engineer representing the employer rightly terminated the contract because of failure of the contractor to perform his contractual obligation.
